## Basic Setup

Every figure in this course starts with one import.

```python
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
```

The commands below all act on "the current figure". You make a figure, add things to it, and
then show it. You do not have to keep track of an object in between.

## Sample Data

The examples use Toolik Lake monthly mean air temperatures, the same table Day 7 plots.

```python
months = ['Jan','Feb','Mar','Apr','May','Jun','Jul','Aug','Sep','Oct','Nov','Dec']
temps = [-22.89, -20.70, -20.69, -11.76, -0.80, 8.59,
         11.22, 7.23, -0.11, -10.54, -18.34, -21.44]
```

## Sizing the Figure

`figsize` is given in inches, as width then height. Start a figure with it whenever the
default proportions do not suit the data.

```python
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 5))
```

## Common Plot Types

### Line plot

Use a line when the x values have a meaningful order, such as time.

```python
plt.plot(months, temps)
```

### Scatter plot

Use a scatter when the x values have no order, and each point is an independent observation.

```python
plt.scatter(bill_length, bill_depth)
```

### Bar plot

```python
plt.bar(months, temps)      # vertical bars
plt.barh(months, temps)     # horizontal bars, easier to read with long category names
```

### Histogram

A histogram takes one sequence of numbers and shows how they are distributed. The bar heights
are counts.

```python
plt.hist(temps, bins=10)
```

## Labelling a Figure

An unlabelled figure is not finished. Axis labels should carry units.

```python
plt.xlabel('Month')
plt.ylabel('Mean air temperature (deg C)')
plt.title('Toolik Lake monthly mean air temperature')
```

## Legends

Give each series a `label=` when you draw it, then call `legend()` once for the whole figure.

```python
plt.plot(months, early_temps, label='1988 to 2002')
plt.plot(months, late_temps, label='2003 to 2018')
plt.legend()
```

## Rotating Tick Labels

When category names collide along the x axis, rotate them. `ha='right'` sets the horizontal
alignment so that the rotated labels line up under their ticks.

```python
plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha='right')
```

## Fixing Crowded Layouts

`tight_layout()` adjusts the spacing so that labels are not cut off. Call it last, just before
showing the figure.

```python
plt.tight_layout()
```

## Showing and Saving

```python
plt.show()                                    # display the figure
plt.savefig('my_plot.png', dpi=300)           # save it to a file
```

Call `savefig()` before `show()`. Showing a figure clears it.

## A Complete Example

```python
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

months = ['Jan','Feb','Mar','Apr','May','Jun','Jul','Aug','Sep','Oct','Nov','Dec']
temps = [-22.89, -20.70, -20.69, -11.76, -0.80, 8.59,
         11.22, 7.23, -0.11, -10.54, -18.34, -21.44]

plt.figure(figsize=(10, 5))
plt.bar(months, temps)
plt.xlabel('Month')
plt.ylabel('Mean air temperature (deg C)')
plt.title('Toolik Lake monthly mean air temperature')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## Plotting from a pandas Series

A grouped result is a Series: its index holds the labels and its values hold the numbers. Pass
those two pieces to any plotting command.

```python
monthly = df.groupby('month')['temp_c'].mean()

plt.figure(figsize=(10, 5))
plt.bar(monthly.index, monthly.values)
plt.xlabel('Month')
plt.ylabel('Mean air temperature (deg C)')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## Matplotlib and Seaborn

These are the only two plotting libraries this course uses. Seaborn draws the figure for you
from a DataFrame, and matplotlib gives you the commands to label and size the result. The two
work on the same figure, so you can call `plt.xlabel()` after `sns.scatterplot()`.

See the [seaborn cheatsheet](seaborn.qmd), the [bar plot cheatsheet](bar_plots.qmd), and the
[matplotlib PDF reference](matplotlib_cheatsheet.pdf).
